hints.title: Binary Exponential Subtraction
hints.text: Repeated subtraction of the divisor is too slow for large inputs. How can bit shifts double the subtracted quantity at each step to achieve logarithmic runtime?

hints.title: Bitwise Multiple Alignment
hints.text: Work with absolute values using 64-bit precision. Left-shift the divisor until it is just below the remaining dividend, subtract, and add the shift power to the quotient.

hints.title: Sign and Clamping Overflow Handling
hints.text: Determine the result sign using exclusive or of sign bits. Clamp the final quotient to the signed 32-bit integer range [minus 2 to 31, 2 to 31 minus 1].

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Linear subtraction of divisor takes O(N) operations, which times out when dividend is 2^31 and divisor is 1.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Exponential binary doubling uses 32 bit iterations with O(1) auxiliary variables.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate must properly handle 32-bit overflow corner cases such as INT_MIN divided by -1.
